Built the playable game in **`index.html`**. It includes a ray-cast 3D arena, enemy waves, shooting and reload mechanics, synthesized sound effects, health and ammo HUD, and a supply-drop menu with upgrades. It also has touch controls for mobile.

**Controls:** WASD to move, mouse to aim, click to fire, R to reload. On mobile, use the joystick, drag to aim, and tap Fire.

Assumption: “multiplayer like Free Fire” is represented as a solo match with a squad-status panel and an AI teammate; this build doesn’t connect to a real online multiplayer service. I checked the game in Chromium and verified the core loop runs without browser errors.

## Objective
- Build a playable 3D shooting game inspired by Free Fire; the user’s follow-up clarifies the desired game should be 3D and online.

## Requirements
- “3d shooting gun online game with sound effects upgrades multiplayer like free fire”
- Follow-up: “3d online game”

## Decisions
- The initial build implemented solo wave-based gameplay with an AI-squad status panel; real online multiplayer was not implemented.
- An attempt is underway to add a Three.js 3D scene alongside the original ray-cast canvas, using PointerLockControls for camera movement.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` contains the original playable ray-cast shooter, HUD, synthesized sound effects, upgrades, waves, and mobile touch controls.
- Verified the original game loop in Chromium without browser errors after fixing `zbuf is not defined`.

### Active
- Integrating an actual Three.js arena and first-person controls into `index.html`.

### Blocked
- The Three.js integration has not been tested; external module imports and interaction with the original canvas/input may fail or conflict.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest changes in `index.html` and run a browser test for module initialization and visible 3D rendering.
2. Resolve canvas layering and reconcile duplicated controls/movement so the 3D scene is the actual game view.
3. Clarify in the final response whether true network multiplayer is implemented; do not imply it is online if it remains local-only.

- `index.html`: all game UI, original 2D ray-cast shooter, and the newly added Three.js scene/module.

- Changes are uncommitted.
- The latest Three.js module imports from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/...`.
- `#world3d` and `#scene` are layered canvases; original rendering/input remains active and may obscure or conflict with the new 3D implementation.
